name: Nuclear risk
value: No US–Russia treaty limits since Feb
summary: No US–Russia arms limits since New START lapsed; Trump, Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen on 19 Nov
state: New START expired in February with no replacement; SIPRI estimates about 5,420 Russian, 5,042 US and 620 Chinese warheads (Deseret News, 16 Nov). China has said it will not join disarmament talks at this stage (Al Jazeera, 16 Nov). Trump plans to raise arms reduction with Xi and Putin in Shenzhen on 19 Nov, though US officials did not expect a deal (Al-Monitor). No test, alert change or threatened use was found as of 19 Nov.
for_you: No direct public guidance applies. Arms-control talks in Shenzhen are worth following.
rubric_hit: Arms-control lapse without replacement (New START) = Watch

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Why is China resisting a nuclear treaty with the US and Russia?

why: Nuclear use anywhere would be a civilisational shock; arms-control treaties are weaker than at any time since the 1960s.
drivers: Threats in active wars, testing, doctrine changes, arms-control collapse, proliferation.

rubric.alert: A nuclear test, changes in deployment/alert levels, or threatened use in an active conflict.
rubric.watch: Explicit threats, unusual exercises, doctrine changes, or arms-control lapses without replacement.
rubric.normal: No explicit nuclear threats or tests; arms-control dialogue active.
